newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi Air to resume scheduled flights after holidays.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Air to resume scheduled flights after holidays.

text.p: Kiwi International Air Lines, having surmounted problems in getting bankruptcy financing, has decided to postpone its return to scheduled flights until after the Christmas holidays, a spokesman said.

Although payments on a $5-million debtor in possession loan are running ahead of schedule, Kiwi spokesman Rob Kulat said, the airline was unable to resume its schedule in time to catch its share of the holiday travel boom.
"Most people who are travelling have already bought their tickets," he said.

Kiwi has been in Chapter 11 protection from creditors since Sept. 30, and a month later announced it had financing from the Boynton Beach, Fla., Wasatch International Group. But it was unable to keep to its promised $500,000 weekly payment schedule.

Wasatch returned to Kiwi Nov. 27 with a partner, an investor group headed by a Baltimore surgeon, Dr. Charles Edwards. The airline has since recalled 20 of its 1,200 employees to manage its charter operations, Kulat said.
Kiwi will continue to charter eight of its 15-jet fleet, he added.
